intro: Botswana went from one of the poorest countries at independence in 1966 to a diamond-rich, stable democracy.

chapters.title: San and Tswana
text: The San people have lived in the Kalahari for tens of thousands of years; the Tsodilo Hills hold thousands of rock paintings. Tswana chiefdoms later formed.

chapters.title: Bechuanaland
text: To avoid takeover by Cecil Rhodes's company, three Tswana chiefs travelled to London in 1895 and asked for British protection. Bechuanaland was lightly ruled by Britain.

chapters.title: Independence and diamonds
text: Seretse Khama led Botswana to independence in 1966. A year later diamonds were found, and the government used the money for roads, schools and clinics. In 2024 the opposition won an election for the first time, and power passed peacefully.

highlight.title: Stable
highlight.text: Botswana has held free elections since independence.

keyTerms.meaning: Indigenous hunter-gatherer peoples of southern Africa.
